name: Darifenacin pivotal trial
question: Does once-daily darifenacin reduce overactive bladder symptoms more than placebo?

design.population: 561 patients aged 19–88 years (85% female) with overactive bladder symptoms for more than 6 months, including some previously exposed to antimuscarinics.

verdictNote: Both formally tested doses improved weekly incontinence; the 3.75 mg arm was not formally tested.
takeaway: In a 12-week randomized trial, once-daily darifenacin 7.5 mg and 15 mg reduced weekly incontinence episodes from baseline more than placebo; the 3.75 mg arm was not formally tested.

reports.label: 12-week primary report
reports.citation: Haab F, Stewart L, Dwyer P. Darifenacin, an M3 selective receptor antagonist, is an effective and well-tolerated once-daily treatment for overactive bladder. *Eur Urol.* 2004;45(4):420-429. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2004.01.008

results.measure: Reduction from baseline at week 12, darifenacin 7.5 mg versus placebo
results.note: The abstract reports a significant between-group comparison but does not give the prespecified alpha or absolute episode counts.

results.measure: Reduction from baseline at week 12, darifenacin 15 mg versus placebo
results.note: The 3.75 mg group was a null-dose arm without formal sample sizing or statistical analysis.

results.measure: Micturition frequency, bladder capacity, urgency frequency and severity, and clothing or pad changes at week 12
results.note: Both tested doses improved these measures; nocturnal awakenings due to OAB did not decline significantly.

harms.label: Constipation-related discontinuation
harms.note: The abstract does not provide dose-specific discontinuation rates or event denominators.

harms.label: Dry mouth and other reported safety findings

values.exp75: Dry mouth and constipation generally mild to moderate; no withdrawal for dry mouth
values.exp15: Dry mouth and constipation generally mild to moderate; no withdrawal for dry mouth
values.ctl: CNS and cardiac profiles described as comparable to darifenacin

harms.note: No blurred vision was reported. The abstract gives no dose-specific adverse-event counts.

delivery.label: Treatment and diary schedule
delivery.value: Controlled-release darifenacin or matching placebo was taken once daily for 12 weeks after washout and a 2-week placebo run-in; electronic diaries preceded visits at weeks 2, 6 and 12.
